u_p(x_n)=
u_p(x_0)+n
u_p(a)\), including \(n=0\), so either all quotients have valuation zero or only the diagonal quotients are units. With \(c\in\mathbb Z_p\), the exact ratio \(x_{n+d}/x_n=a^d+da^d/(n+c)\), Euler exponent choices, and dense positive integers construct approximants to every element of \(\mathbb Q_p\). The zero-root and zero-slope cases are separately excluded. Finite tests of 891 recurrences, 460 valuation cases and 23 rational approximants supplement the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: Antony–Barman (2022), Theorem 1.7, establishes only \(p\nmid aD\) as a sufficient density condition for the same recurrence; the 2024 follow-up does not remove \(p\nmid a\) for arbitrary initial data. Garcia et al. (2016) cover special canonical initial values. Those results do not entail the sharp if-and-only-if criterion for all exceptional primes. Targeted published-literature and research-record comparisons found no implication-equivalent theorem, but an unindexed equivalent formulation remains a risk.
residual_risks: A differently stated unpublished or unindexed elementary classification might imply the same result.
The foundational papers have related general density lemmas; the comparison addresses their implications for this particular full classification, not priority outside the inspected literature.

value.rationale: The theorem completely answers the prime-by-prime quotient-density problem for the repeated-root order-two integer family singled out in a published sufficient-condition theorem. The sharp integrality cutoff \(\nu_p(a x_0)\ge\nu_p(x_1-a x_0)\) distinguishes dense from non-dense initial data even for \(p\mid a(x_1-a x_0)\). This is an infinite structural classification, not an arbitrary finite enumeration.
